bib.title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 2978-2988

read.skipped: Nothing skipped. The PDF is the 11-page ACL version and contains no appendices, although the text refers to Appendices A (Table 10), B, C and E; their content (hyperparameters, RECL definition, samples) is not in the file.

question: Can a self-attention language model learn dependencies beyond a fixed-length context without context fragmentation, and be faster to evaluate?
hypothesis: Segment-level recurrence with cached hidden states, combined with relative positional encodings, captures longer dependency than RNNs and vanilla Transformers and resolves context fragmentation.
contributions: Segment-level recurrence with state reuse in a purely self-attentive model
A relative positional encoding formulation that generalizes to attention lengths longer than seen in training
A new metric, Relative Effective Context Length (RECL)
New state-of-the-art on enwik8, text8, WikiText-103, One Billion Word and Penn Treebank (without finetuning)

method.summary: Transformer-XL caches the previous segment's hidden states (stop-gradient) as memory that keys and values attend over, and replaces absolute position embeddings with a sinusoidal relative encoding plus two learned global bias vectors u and v and separate key matrices for content and position. Trained as a language model on five benchmarks, with ablations on recurrence and encoding, RECL, and evaluation speed against the vanilla Transformer of Al-Rfou et al.

training.objective: autoregressive next-token cross-entropy; no auxiliary losses (stated for enwik8). Ablations compare Full (loss on all positions) and Half (loss on the recent half of positions in the segment)

training.seq_len: memory length M equals segment length during training; backpropagation length 128 in the WikiText-103 ablation
training.dropout: variational dropout on Penn Treebank; rates not stated
training.regularisation: variational dropout and weight average for Penn Treebank

other.hyperparameters: deferred to released code; no appendix in this PDF

parameters.memory_length_eval: M increased by multiple times over training at evaluation (WikiText-103 attention 1600, enwik8 3,800)

metrics.name: perplexity (PPL)
metrics.definition: exp of average per-token negative log-likelihood; word-level datasets

metrics.name: bits per character (bpc)
metrics.definition: average per-character negative log-likelihood in bits; enwik8, text8

metrics.name: Relative Effective Context Length (RECL)
metrics.definition: defined on a model group; gain of a long context is the relative improvement over the best short-context model in the group, restricted to the top-r hard examples (full definition in Appendix C, not in this PDF)

metrics.name: evaluation slowdown
metrics.definition: per-token evaluation time of Al-Rfou et al. relative to Transformer-XL on one GPU

baselines: LSTM, TCN, GCNN, QRNN, AWD-LSTM, MoS and other RNN/CNN LMs
Shaw et al. (2018) and Vaswani et al. (2017) positional encodings in ablation
eval.protocol: single reported run per setting; no seeds or significance tests stated

evidence.quote: We set the attention length to 384 during training and 1600 during evaluation.

results.claim: Transformer-XL Large reaches 18.3 test perplexity on WikiText-103, against 20.5 for contemporary Adaptive Input.
results.setup: WikiText-103, 257M-parameter Transformer-XL Large, attention length 384 train / 1600 eval; baseline Adaptive Input is 247M and is contemporary work. The 151M Standard model gets 24.0.
results.table: Table 1, row Ours - Transformer-XL Large, column PPL (18.3); row Baevski and Auli (2018) - Adaptive Input (20.5)

results.claim: A 24-layer Transformer-XL reaches 0.99 bpc on enwik8, the first below 1.0.
results.setup: enwik8, 24L, 277M parameters, attention length 784 train / 3,800 eval; baseline is the 64L 235M Al-Rfou Transformer at 1.06.
results.table: Table 2, row Ours - 24L Transformer-XL, column bpc (0.99); row Al-Rfou et al. (2018) - 64L Transformer (1.06)

results.claim: A 12-layer Transformer-XL matches the 64-layer vanilla Transformer on enwik8 with 17% of the parameters.
results.setup: enwik8, 12L Transformer-XL (41M) vs 12L Al-Rfou (44M, 1.11) and 64L Al-Rfou (235M, 1.06).
results.table: Table 2, row Ours - 12L Transformer-XL, column bpc (1.06); row Al-Rfou et al. (2018) - 12L Transformer (1.11)
results.note: Text says it uses only 17% of the parameter budget of the 64L network.

results.claim: 24-layer Transformer-XL reaches 1.08 bpc on text8, with enwik8 hyper-parameters and no tuning.
results.table: Table 3, row Ours - 24L Transformer-XL, column bpc (1.08); row Al-Rfou et al. (2018) - 64L Transformer (1.13)

results.claim: On One Billion Word, which has no long-term dependency, Transformer-XL Large improves the single-model state of the art from 23.7 to 21.8.
results.setup: One Billion Word, Transformer-XL Large 0.8B; Base 0.46B gets 23.5; baseline Adaptive Input 1.0B (contemporary).
results.table: Table 4, row Ours - Transformer-XL Large, column PPL (21.8); row Adaptive Input 1.0B (23.7)
results.note: Table 4 also lists Shazeer et al. 2018 Mesh Tensorflow at 24.0.

results.claim: Transformer-XL gets 54.52 perplexity on Penn Treebank among models without two-step finetuning.
results.setup: Penn Treebank, 24M parameters, variational dropout and weight average; MoS+Finetune gets 54.44 with two-step finetuning.
results.table: Table 5, row Ours - Transformer-XL, column PPL (54.52); row Melis et al. (2018) - Dropout tuning (55.3)

results.claim: Ablation on One Billion Word: removing recurrence raises perplexity from 25.2 to 27.1, and Shaw et al. encodings give 25.7.
results.setup: One Billion Word, 20-layer Transformer-XL of about 0.3B parameters, 400K steps.
results.table: Table 7, row Without recurrence, column PPL (27.1); row Ours (25.2)

results.claim: WikiText-103 ablation: with recurrence and the proposed encoding (128M), perplexity falls from 27.02 at training length to 26.77 at attention length 500; without recurrence, Shaw or absolute encodings gain nothing from longer attention.
results.setup: WikiText-103, 128M model, backpropagation length 128, full loss.
results.table: Table 6, first row (Recurrence yes, Ours, Full), columns PPL init 27.02, PPL best 26.77, Attn Len 500

results.claim: In the standard 151M setting, WikiText-103 perplexity decreases as attention length grows to 640 at test time though backpropagation length is 128.
results.setup: WikiText-103, 151M, Ours encoding, Full loss, attention length 640 vs training length.
results.table: Table 6, row Transformer-XL (151M), columns PPL init 23.43 and PPL best 23.09
results.note: Same row lists 23.16 at 450 and 23.35 at 300.

results.claim: RECL: Transformer-XL 151M models dependency of 900 words at r = 0.1, 80% longer than recurrent networks and 450% longer than Transformer.
results.setup: Compared within parameter-matched model groups; LSTM 400, QRNN 500 and vanilla Transformer 128 at r = 0.1. Group of 128M models: Transformer-XL 700, Shaw 400, no recurrence 300.
results.table: Table 8, row Transformer-XL 151M, column r = 0.1 (900); row LSTM (400)
results.note: Text gives 80% and 450%; the pairing behind them is not spelled out (900 vs QRNN 500 is 80%).

results.claim: Evaluation is up to 1,874 times faster than the vanilla Transformer of Al-Rfou et al. at attention length 3,800; 363x at 800.
results.setup: Per-token evaluation time on one GPU, at attention lengths 800 to 3,800.
results.quote: Transformer-XL achieves an up to 1,874 times speedup during evaluation.

limits: The PDF has no appendices: optimizer, learning rate, batch size, layers/width for most models, training steps, hardware and the RECL definition are not in it.
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests.
Adaptive Input baselines are contemporary work; Transformer-XL Large models are larger than most baselines.
R is a fixed sinusoid with no learnable parameters; no clipping of relative distance is described.
Word-level Transformer-XL results use adaptive softmax and inputs; the effect is not ablated.

terms.definition: fixed-length segments are created by selecting a consecutive chunk of symbols without respecting the sentence or any other semantic boundary, so the model lacks context for the first few symbols
hidden states computed for the previous segment are fixed and cached to be reused as an extended context for the next segment, with the gradient staying within a segment
defined on a model group; the gain of a long context is measured by relative improvement over the best short context model, constrained to the top-r hard examples

lineage.note: Effective context length, which RECL refines
